title: Who Does What on a Film Set
objective: After this level you can explain the jobs of the director, producer, cinematographer, gaffer, grip and script supervisor.
summary: The producer runs the money, the director the vision, the cinematographer the camera, the gaffer and grips the light, and the script supervisor continuity.

cards.headline: The campfire in a movie scene might be nothing but lights.
cards.body: When a scene calls for a campfire that can't really be built on set, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics explains, gaffers use lights to recreate a fire's flicker. That's one job among many. A film set runs on specialists, so here's who does what.

cards.headline: Producer and director: the business and the vision
cards.body: Producers are a film's managers, from securing the money in pre-production to approving the finished film. They hire the director, create the budget and approve changes to the script, budget or schedule. The director develops the film's artistic vision: helping choose the cast, overseeing the shooting of each scene, guiding the actors and working closely with the cinematographer.

cards.headline: Camera and light: cinematographer, gaffer, grip
cards.body: The cinematographer, also called the director of photography, is in charge of shooting the scenes and decides how the camera moves to serve the director's vision. The AFI adds that they choose the camera, the lenses and how to light each scene. The gaffer, the chief electrician, designs and adjusts each scene's lighting scheme. Grips carry out that lighting plan and can support the camera on a dolly or crane.

cards.headline: The script supervisor: keeper of continuity
cards.body: A film is shot take after take, and the pieces must fit when they're cut together. The script supervisor keeps the record: slate numbers, notes on each take, lenses, the action and running times, plus props, makeup and costumes. The BFI calls continuity something that, by its nature, should be entirely invisible. If you never notice it, it worked.

cards.headline: The film crew: introduced
learned: Producer: money, budget and schedule, start to finish
Director: the artistic vision and the actors
Cinematographer, gaffer, grips: camera and light
Script supervisor: records every take so pieces fit

questions.prompt: The _____ is the chief electrician who designs each scene's lighting scheme.

options.label: grip
options.rationale: Grips carry out the gaffer's lighting plan.

options.label: script supervisor
options.rationale: The script supervisor keeps continuity records.

options.label: producer
options.rationale: The producer manages money and schedule.

questions.explanation: The gaffer is the chief electrician; gaffers design and adjust the lighting scheme for each scene.

questions.prompt: Match each crew member with their job.
questions.explanation: The producer creates the budget, the director develops the film's artistic vision, the gaffer is the chief electrician, and the script supervisor is the keeper of continuity.

questions.prompt: In Level 21, development ends with someone looking for money. Which crew member is that?

options.label: The director
options.rationale: The director shapes the artistic vision, not the financing.

options.label: The cinematographer
options.rationale: The cinematographer is in charge of shooting the scenes.

questions.explanation: Producers secure the financing and manage the film from pre-production to final approval.
